thread:
rachel: Heads-up 15: planning doc for the Optimize toolkit pilot (recommendation telemetry + rollout phasing). Want quick alignment before I spin up the RFC.

diego: Ping. Key tradeoff: how prescriptive are we vs how much telemetry we collect. Customers worry about data sent back.

maya: Agreed. Propose minimal telemetry by default: model id, request hash (no raw prompt), latency, token count, chosen config. Opt-in raw prompt capture for pilot only with NDA.

sam: For launch gating we should define two signal tiers: safety signals (semantic drift, hallucination spikes) and econ signals (cost delta, throughput). Safety gating must be hard stop.
rachel: Good. What are numeric thresholds we feel comfortable with for v1?

maya: Suggested econ targets: expected median cost reduction >= 8% across sampled workloads; 95th percentile latency increase <= 20ms; 99th percentile tail not worse than baseline. Safety: BLEU/perplexity delta < 2% on baseline evals and human review pass rate >= 95%.
diego: Can we also require model-specific quant rules? e.g., for gpt-core-7b allow int8 but require post-quant eval; for transformer-xxl block int4 in v1.
sam: Yes. We'll maintain a whitelist with per-model allowed precisions + mandatory eval script run. Add a "reason" and "confidence" field to each rec so UX can surface why we suggested it.
rachel: UX question: console cards vs API vs CSV export? Which do customers ask for most?
maya: Most want API so they can integrate into ops playbooks. But ship console cards for quick visibility, and CSV export for procurement/legal teams.
diego: Rollout plan: phase 0 = internal-only (sandbox), phase 1 = invited customers (opt-in), phase 2 = wider public read-only, phase 3 = autopilot experiments (future).
sam: For invited customers we should require an A/B test scaffold: 50/50 split, 2 week run, key metrics: tokens/second, avg cost per 1k tokens, quality regression on eval set.
rachel: Who owns the A/B analysis? @maya metrics, @sam eval, @diego infra for routing and experiment flags.

data-bot: Created experiment EXP-7421: "Optimize toolkit pilot - invited A/B test". Dashboard: https://redwood.internal/exp/EXP-7421

maya: Telemetry export schema sketch (CSV) - saving here as a snippet:

request_id, model, rec_type, rec_detail, baseline_latency_ms, rec_latency_ms, baseline_cost_usd, rec_cost_usd, quality_signal, confidence, opt_in_note
abc123,gpt-core-7b,quantize,int8,120,95,0.0045,0.0036,0.99,0.82,NDA

diego: Good. Add a field for "post_eval_status" (pass/fail) and "human_review_id" for traceability.
sam: Also store a small diff summary for logits/perplexity for internal debugging (no raw tokens).
rachel: Messaging: call this "recommendations" and be explicit that v1 will not change deployments automatically. Use conservative copy in console: "Suggested configuration based on observed workload; opt-in required."
maya: Timeline: RFC + perf targets by Tue, pilot infra by Fri, invite customers next Mon.
diego: I'll scope infra tasks and put in ENG-5412.
sam: I'll finalize the eval harness and sample human review rubric.
rachel: Thanks team. If no objections by EOD I'm going to publish the RFC. Post any blockers here.
maya: No blockers from metrics.
diego: One minor infra dependency on a routing flag; otherwise good.
sam: No blockers.
rachel: Okay publishing tomorrow then.
